full_judgment:
An advertisement for admission test for all Government and Non-Government Medical Colleges was published in "The Daily Prothorn Alo" on 31-8-2013. In the said advertisement, it was clearly stipulated that only those students who took science subjects and scored Grade Point Average (GPA) of minimum 8-00 in his/her SSC and HSC Examinations with at least GPA-3.5 in either of the aforementioned examinations are eligible to sit for the admission test. The petitioner having the abovementioned required score sat for the admission test for MBBS course for the session 2013-2014. The result of the admission test was published online and made available to everybody. In the result sheet, her name appeared at serial No. 1712 having roll No. 201818 and she scored 109.38 out of 200 marks. She applied to the respondent No. 8-BGC Trust Medical College, Chandanaish, Chittagong for admission to 1st year, MBBS course and accordingly she submitted all the relevant papers and documents required therefor. Thereafter she was admitted to 1st year, MBBS course for the session 2013-2014 and began her studies in the college. Meanwhile she completed her 3rd year MBBS course and passed the 1st Professional Course Examination. All of a sudden, during the 2nd Professional Course Examination around May 2017, she was notified by the respondent No. 8 that the respondents had raised questions about her admission qualification. In fact, the entire admission procedure was completed by the respondent No. 8 based on all the original papers and documents submitted at the time of application for admission to the college including the admission test result sheet published online which were checked and verified by the college authority. Having being fully satisfied, the respondent No. 8 forwarded those to the respondent No. 4 (Directorate of Health Services). Having been found everything in order, the Bangladesh Medical and Dental Council (respondent No. 2) recommended the petitioner to the respondent No. 5-Chittagong University for issuance of registration in her favour. Accordingly on compliance with all necessary formalities, the Chittagong University found the petitioner eligible for admission as a student of MBBS course and gave her registration/identification No. 550 of 2013-2014 session. 

 7. Be that as it may, at the instance of one Mamunur Rashid, a senior journalist of "The Daily Samakal", necessary inquiries were held and ultimately it was found that the petitioner had scored 109.38 in place of 127.38 out of 200 marks in the admission test. In other words, as per the advertisement for admission to the medical college, the petitioner was disqualified for admission in view of the fact that she had scored 109.38 marks which were below the benchmark of 120. Afterwards the respondent No. 8 received a letter dated 6-7-2017 from the respondent No. 3 stating that no registration would be accorded to the petitioner. After receipt of the said letter dated 6-7-2017 from the respondent No. 3, the respondent No. 8 by a notice dated 12-7-2017 asked the petitioner to show cause as to why her admission should not be cancelled for submitting discrepant documents at the time of her admission. The petitioner replied to the show cause notice by a letter dated 18-7-2017; but the reply was found unsatisfactory. Thereafter the Chittagong University by its letter dated 18-7-2017 informed the respondent No. 8 of the cancellation of admission and registration of the petitioner for getting herself admitted to the medical college by submitting forged and fabricated documents. Then the respondent No. 8 by its letter dated 24-7-2017 cancelled the admission of the petitioner. The medical college authority was misled by the petitioner on production of forged and fraudulent documents at the time of her admission to MBBS course for the session 2013-2014. The college authority was never a party to the fraud committed by the petitioner. So the Rule is liable to be discharged with costs.
